title: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith
body:
Read the chapter → [Galatians 2](/bible/galatians/2)

**[Galatians 2:1-2](/bible/galatians/2#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/galatians/2#v1)</sup> Then fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also. And I went up by revelation, and communicated unto them that gospel which I preached among the Gentiles, but privately to them which were of reputation, lest by any means I should run, or had run, in vain.

- This is Paul's second visit to Jerusalem, 14 years after his first trip (which was 3 years after his conversion on the road to Damascus). Paul went up by revelation, meaning the spirit of the Lord led him to Jerusalem.
- The majority of Paul's epistles and the issues he addresses extend around the history of Acts chapter 15. In Acts 15:1, certain men from Judea taught the brethren that unless you are circumcised after the manner of Moses, you cannot be saved.
- This meant getting circumcised to reestablish the covenant with Abraham and giving an animal sacrifice to reestablish the covenant of Moses. Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them over this, so they were sent to the apostles and elders in Jerusalem.
- Acts 15:3 says they passed through Phenice and Samaria declaring the conversion of the Gentiles. Acts 15:4 shows when they came to Jerusalem, they were received by the church, apostles, and elders, and declared all things God had done with them. 'Privately to them which were of reputation' refers to the apostles and elders. 'Lest by any means I should run or had run in vain' means Paul had to check with the leadership to confirm he was on the right path.
- There were always checks and balances. The leadership would steer you in the right direction.

  Precepts:
  - **[Acts 15:1-4](/bible/acts/15#v1)**
  - **[Galatians 1:18](/bible/galatians/1#v18)**


**[Galatians 2:3-4](/bible/galatians/2#v3)**

> <sup>[3](/bible/galatians/2#v3)</sup> But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised: And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage:

- Titus being a Greek means he was brought up in Greek customs and fashion, just like Timothy whose father was a Greek. He was not a Caucasian.
- He was an Israelite raised in Greek ways. 'Was compelled to be circumcised' shows the Pharisees were going around forcefully telling people they had to be circumcised and return to animal sacrifice. The false brethren brought in unawares are identified in Acts 15:5: 'there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying that it was needful to circumcise them and to command them to keep the law of Moses.' These were believers who infiltrated the congregation with this doctrine.
- Titus was one of those drawn away by this false doctrine. He eventually forsook Paul: 2 Timothy 4:10 says 'Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world..
- Titus unto Dalmatia.' Titus was an elder of the highest rank. Titus 1:4-5 shows Paul called him 'mine own son after the common faith' and charged him to ordain elders in every city.
- Yet even Titus, who had a book written after him, fell away through these doctrines about circumcision and animal sacrifice. If Titus could fall, anybody could fall.
- Paul warns in 1 Corinthians 9:27 that he keeps his body under subjection lest he himself become a castaway.

  Precepts:
  - **[Acts 15:5](/bible/acts/15#v5)**
  - **[2 Timothy 4:10](/bible/2-timothy/4#v10)**
  - **[Titus 1:4-5](/bible/titus/1#v4)**
  - **[1 Corinthians 9:27](/bible/1-corinthians/9#v27)**


**Why Peter switched to the Gentiles topic**


- In Acts 15:7-9, after the dispute about circumcision and animal sacrifice, Peter switches to the topic of the Gentiles. The reason: if salvation required circumcision and animal sacrifice (the old covenant), then the northern kingdom (called Gentiles, strangers, heathens) could never receive salvation.
- They were strangers from the covenants of promise (Ephesians 2:12). The northern kingdom was excommunicated because Jeroboam prohibited them from going to Jerusalem to sacrifice (1 Kings 12:26-29).
- He set up two golden calves and created his own priests and high holy days, causing the northern kingdom to worship idols and be exiled. Tobit 1:3-8 confirms this history: all the tribe of Naphtali fell from the house of Jerusalem, though Tobit alone went often to Jerusalem at the feasts.
- John 4:20-22 records the Samaritan woman saying 'Our fathers worshipped in this mountain,' referring to the northern kingdom's worship of false gods, and Christ replied 'Ye worship ye know not what.. salvation is of the Jews.' Deuteronomy 12:5-7 commands all tribes to bring burnt offerings and sacrifices to the place the Lord chose, which was Jerusalem. So if animal sacrifice were still in effect, the northern kingdom could never be grafted back in because they broke the covenants of promise.
- Only through Christ could all 12 tribes receive salvation.

  Precepts:
  - **[Acts 15:7-10](/bible/acts/15#v7)**
  - **[Ephesians 2:12-16](/bible/ephesians/2#v12)**
  - **[1 Kings 12:26-29](/bible/1-kings/12#v26)**
  - **[Tobit 1:3-8](/bible/tobit/1#v3)**
  - **[John 4:20-22](/bible/john/4#v20)**
  - **[Deuteronomy 12:5-7](/bible/deuteronomy/12#v5)**

**The yoke of animal sacrifice (Acts 15:10)**


> Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?

- The yoke Peter speaks of in Acts 15:10 is the covenant of animal sacrifice. A yoke is an instrument used to keep you captive, subjected, imprisoned.
- Israel was bound under the curses because of the animal sacrifice covenant. When we broke God's laws, the curses fell upon us: death, disease, captivity, murder, rape, oppression, poverty.
- Hebrews 8:6-9 shows Christ is the mediator of a better covenant established upon better promises (immortality, the eternal kingdom). If the first covenant (animal sacrifice) had been faultless, there would be no need for a second.
- God found fault with the people and made a new covenant with both the house of Israel and the house of Judah. Hebrews 9:8-10 explains that animal sacrifice was temporary, a figure for that time period: it stood only in meats, drinks, diverse washings, and carnal ordinances imposed until the time of reformation.
- Animal sacrifice could not make a person perfect because there were certain sins (homosexuality, adultery, murder, witchcraft) for which you were put to death with no atonement. Under Christ, we receive mercy and the opportunity to overcome sin.
- That is why Christ is called the end of the law (of sacrifice) to them that believe. Ephesians 2:14-16 shows Christ broke down the middle wall of partition between the two kingdoms, abolishing in his flesh the enmity (the law of commandments contained in ordinances, meaning the sacrificial laws), making of twain one new man.

  Precepts:
  - **[Hebrews 8:6-9](/bible/hebrews/8#v6)**
  - **[Hebrews 9:8-10](/bible/hebrews/9#v8)**
  - **[Ephesians 2:14-16](/bible/ephesians/2#v14)**
  - **[2 Esdras 2:40](/bible/2-esdras/2#v40)**

**[Galatians 2:4 (continued) - False brethren and 1 John 2:18-19](/bible/galatians/2#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/galatians/2#v4)</sup> And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage:

- The liberty in Christ Jesus is grace and mercy. The false brethren were able to subvert believers from the gospel and persuade them outside of what they learned. 1 John 2:18-19 says 'Little children, it is the last time: and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists.' Antichrist is anybody against the mission or doctrine of Christ.
- John says they went out from us, from the disciples, from the congregations and churches. If they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us, but they went out that they might be made manifest.
- Many of the deceivers and heretics come from the body itself, from those who are bitter and hold grudges. You cannot fake this truth forever.
- Eventually, if you are not of the elect, it will be manifest in your spirit and you will leave. The same thing happened in the apostles' time is happening today under different names but the same spirits.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 John 2:18-19](/bible/1-john/2#v18)**
  - **[1 Corinthians 9:27](/bible/1-corinthians/9#v27)**


**[Galatians 2:5](/bible/galatians/2#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/galatians/2#v5)</sup> To whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you.

- Paul says the disciples did not give place to the heretics, not even for one hour. As soon as they heard the heresy, they said you have to go.
- Paul reads Psalms 51 every day, praying to endure and not become a castaway. The disciples did not give time for heretics to spread their doctrine because they understood there are weak-minded people in the body that are easily deceived.
- Any heretical doctrine brought into the congregation is dealt with immediately. You come with any type of doctrines into the congregation, you will be removed.
- The disciples did not debate heretics. They did not argue with them.
- This is how the truth of the gospel continues with the people.

  Precepts:
  - **[Psalms 51](/bible/psalms/51)**


**[Galatians 2:6](/bible/galatians/2#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/galatians/2#v6)</sup> But of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth no man's person:) for they who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to me.

- Paul says these people pushing false doctrine seemed to be somebody, puffed up, of nobility and specialty. But Paul said it made no matter to him.
- They took some people from the congregation and felt good about themselves, but it did not harm the apostles. God accepted no man's person, meaning God does not care about these people who left.
- He would use you then cast you away. They who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to Paul.
- They did not do the apostles any harm. They did themselves harm.
- They were not fighting against the disciples but fighting against God. The class ends with Paul noting they covered verses 1 through 6, and next week they will continue from verse 7 through 21.


**[Galatians 2:7-8](/bible/galatians/2#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/galatians/2#v7)</sup> But contrariwise, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter; (For he that wrought effectually in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles:)

- Paul's ministry was given to him by Christ and was directed to the uncircumcision, just as Peter's ministry was to the circumcision, also wrought by Christ. The uncircumcision was also called the Gentiles; these terms mean one and the same.
- In Acts 11:1, the apostles heard that the Gentiles had received the word of God, referring specifically to Cornelius. In Acts 10:31-36, Peter explains his encounter with Cornelius.
- Acts 10:35 says in every nation he that fears God and works righteousness is accepted with Him. Verse 36 clarifies: the word which God sent unto the children of Israel.
- This cuts any doubt about Cornelius being of another nation. James 1:1 confirms the 12 tribes were scattered abroad throughout all nations starting from the Assyrian captivity onward.
- In Acts 11:2-3, those of the circumcision contended with Peter for going to men uncircumcised. Romans 3:1 shows the Jews were called the circumcision because they kept the covenant of circumcision established to Abraham.
- The circumcision was the southern kingdom of Judah, Benjamin, and Levi. The uncircumcised were primarily the northern kingdom.

  Precepts:
  - **[Acts 11:1-3](/bible/acts/11#v1)**
  - **[Acts 10:31-36](/bible/acts/10#v31)**
  - **[Romans 3:1](/bible/romans/3#v1)**
  - **[James 1:1](/bible/james/1#v1)**
  - **[Ezekiel 37:22](/bible/ezekiel/37#v22)**
  - **[Acts 10:28](/bible/acts/10#v28)**


**why northern kingdom was uncircumcised**


- 1 Maccabees 1:41-48 shows that King Antiochus commanded all kingdoms to be one people under one government and religion (Hellenization). Many Israelites consented to the king's religion, sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the Sabbath.
- Verse 48 specifically says they were commanded to leave their children uncircumcised. 2 Maccabees 6:6 says it was not lawful for a man to keep Sabbath days or ancient feasts or to profess himself to be a Jew. 2 Maccabees 6:10 records that two women who circumcised their children were led around the city and cast down headlong from the wall with their babies. Israelite women were killed for circumcising their children.
- This is why the northern kingdom Israelites in Acts 11:3 are called uncircumcised: they were not allowed to circumcise during the Greek captivity.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Maccabees 1:41-48](/bible/1-maccabees/1#v41)**
  - **[2 Maccabees 6:6](/bible/2-maccabees/6#v6)**
  - **[2 Maccabees 6:10](/bible/2-maccabees/6#v10)**

**[Galatians 2:9](/bible/galatians/2#v9)**

> <sup>[9](/bible/galatians/2#v9)</sup> And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.

- When Paul came to Jerusalem, the apostles perceived the Most High was dealing with him based on his ministry and the people he was waking up. You can tell the spirit on someone by how they move.
- If the spirit of the Most High is in you, it compels you to keep pushing forward in the truth no matter how tired or exhausted. Those who are faking it can only do it for so long before they pull back, become less visible, and eventually leave.
- Verse 9 introduces a third term: the heathen. Paul was sent to the heathen, same people called uncircumcision and Gentiles.
- Ezekiel 20:31-32 shows God rebukes Israel for idolatry and says Israel declared 'we will be as the heathen' by following other nations' customs. When Israelites go outside their laws and follow other nations, they are called heathens.
- Ezekiel 25:8 shows even other nations recognized when Israel became like the heathen. 2 Esdras 2:33-34 records Ezra calling Israel 'ye heathen' because they set the commandments of God at naught. Acts 15:22-23 confirms this: the apostles sent letters to 'the brethren which are of the Gentiles' in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia.
- They are called brethren of the Gentiles. Romans 9:3-4 proves the apostles' brethren are Israelites.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ezekiel 20:31-32](/bible/ezekiel/20#v31)**
  - **[Ezekiel 25:8](/bible/ezekiel/25#v8)**

  - **[Acts 15:22-23](/bible/acts/15#v22)**
  - **[Romans 9:1-4](/bible/romans/9#v1)**
  - **[1 Peter 2:5](/bible/1-peter/2#v5)**


**[Galatians 2:10](/bible/galatians/2#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/galatians/2#v10)</sup> Only they would that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do.

- Acts 15:22 shows this encounter that Paul is explaining to the Galatians. The apostles and elders sent chosen men (Judas surnamed Barsabas and Silas, chief men among the brethren) with Paul and Barnabas to Antioch.
- They were given a charge to go to the brethren of the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia.

  Precepts:
  - **[Acts 15:22-23](/bible/acts/15#v22)**

**[Galatians 2:11-13](/bible/galatians/2#v11)**

> <sup>[11](/bible/galatians/2#v11)</sup> But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision. And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation.

- This history is not recorded in Acts. After Paul was in Antioch doing his ministry, Peter came along later.
- Paul confronted Peter to his face because he was at fault. Peter, being the head apostle and second in command from Christ, still made mistakes.
- Before certain men came from James, Peter ate with the Gentiles (Israelites living in a Gentile way of life). But when the southern kingdom arrived, Peter withdrew and separated himself from the northern kingdom out of respect of persons.
- He did not want to be seen eating with them. The other Jews also dissembled with him, and even Barnabas was carried away, withdrawing himself from the northern kingdom, not sitting or eating with them.
- Peter was being a hypocrite: he feared the circumcision (southern kingdom) and showed respect of persons.


**[Galatians 2:14](/bible/galatians/2#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/galatians/2#v14)</sup> But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?

- Paul confronted Peter in front of everybody. He said: you claim to be a Jew, salvation is of the Jews, and you are supposed to be an example, but you are doing the same thing the northern kingdom was doing.
- You are following their footsteps rather than being an example. You are showing respect of persons and living like them while trying to teach them to follow after the Jews.
- You are being a hypocrite in your actions. Paul did not let things slide.
- He had no respect of persons and did not fear any man regardless of their status.


**[Galatians 2:15](/bible/galatians/2#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/galatians/2#v15)</sup> We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles,

- Being Jews by nature means being born as a Jew and keeping the laws by nature. They are not like the Gentiles being sinners (breaking the law).

**[Galatians 2:16](/bible/galatians/2#v16)**

> <sup>[16](/bible/galatians/2#v16)</sup> Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.

- This is a very famous scripture used by Christians to argue against keeping the law. But Paul is making reference to a specific law.
- Romans 2:13 says 'the doers of the law shall be justified,' which refers to the commandments (as shown by Romans 2:17-22 listing do not steal, do not commit adultery, abhor idols). So we ARE justified by keeping the commandments.
- But in Galatians 2:16, 'the works of the law' refers to a different law. Acts 13:38-39 clarifies: through Christ is preached forgiveness of sins, and all that believe are justified from all things from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses.
- Under the law of Moses (animal sacrifice), you could not be justified for certain sins like homosexuality, adultery, witchcraft: you were put to death. Hebrews 10:4-8 proves it: it is not possible that the blood of bulls and goats should take away sins.
- Animal sacrifice was temporary. When Christ came, sacrifice and offerings were no longer in effect because Christ would be the ultimate sacrifice.
- We were not justified by the sacrificial law, but by Christ. Sirach 42:15 confirms that the works of the Lord are His law, statutes, and commandments.
- Exodus 18:20 says 'show them the way wherein they must walk, and the work that they must do,' meaning the ordinances and the laws. Isaiah 45:25 prophesied that in the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified.
- Habakkuk 2:4 says the just shall live by his faith, meaning the justified seed of Israel shall live by faith in Christ rather than by animal sacrifice.

  Precepts:
  - **[Romans 2:13](/bible/romans/2#v13)**

  - **[Exodus 18:20](/bible/exodus/18#v20)**
  - **[Deuteronomy 22:22](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v22)**


**[Galatians 2:17](/bible/galatians/2#v17)**

> <sup>[17](/bible/galatians/2#v17)</sup> But if, while we seek to be justified by Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners, is therefore Christ the minister of sin? God forbid.

- Even when seeking to be justified by Christ, we are still found sinners because sin is the transgression of the law (1 John 3:4). Even under Christ, if you break the law, you are a sinner. 'Is therefore Christ the minister of sin?' means: did Christ teach us to break the law?
- No. Christ taught us to keep the law.
- Romans 6:1 says shall we continue in sin that grace may abound? God forbid.
- You cannot take advantage of grace and continue breaking the law. This verse is a perfect scripture to combat anyone who says we are not justified by the law: by saying you are not justified by the law, you are saying Christ teaches us to sin.
- Proverbs 24:16 also applies: a just man falls seven times and rises up again.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 John 3:4](/bible/1-john/3#v4)**
  - **[Romans 6:1](/bible/romans/6#v1)**
  - **[Proverbs 24:16](/bible/proverbs/24#v16)**


**[Galatians 2:18](/bible/galatians/2#v18)**

> <sup>[18](/bible/galatians/2#v18)</sup> For if I build again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor.

- If you used to be a fornicator or adulterer and you overcame those sins but then go back into them, you are building again the things you destroyed. You made provision for the flesh and went back into old sins.
- You become a transgressor just like you were from the beginning. All the work you did in overcoming sin was for naught.


**[Galatians 2:19](/bible/galatians/2#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/galatians/2#v19)</sup> For I through the law am dead to the law, that I might live unto God.

- Through the law of animal sacrifice, Paul is now dead to the law of animal sacrifice, that he might live unto God. Romans 7:4 confirms: 'ye also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ.' We are dead to the law of animal sacrifice by the body of Christ because Christ laid down his life for us.

  Precepts:
  - **[Romans 7:4](/bible/romans/7#v4)**


**[Galatians 2:20](/bible/galatians/2#v20)**

> <sup>[20](/bible/galatians/2#v20)</sup> I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.

- The old man is crucified with Christ. Even though Paul lives in the flesh, Christ lives in him.
- Christ gave him the opportunity and chance to repent and receive forgiveness of sins. Living by faith in Christ means living under His grace and mercies, believing that Christ died for our sins, rather than believing in the law of animal sacrifice.


**[Galatians 2:21](/bible/galatians/2#v21)**

> <sup>[21](/bible/galatians/2#v21)</sup> I do not frustrate the grace of God: for if righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain.

- Paul says he will not frustrate the grace of God, meaning he will not prevent God's grace from coming to fruition by pushing animal sacrifice or going against Christ. If righteousness comes by the law of animal sacrifice, then Christ the Messiah died in vain.
- All the prophecies pertaining to Christ coming and dying for our sins would be for nothing if we continue in the law of animal sacrifice.
